notes: Identity independently confirmed: supplied canonical text is the full primary Original Article, Brons, Liefbroer and Ganzeboom, European Sociological Review 33(6), 809–822 (2017), exact title and DOI 10.1093/esr/jcx078 match the neutral original reference. Text contains methods, results, figures, discussion and references; provenance header names an OSF download. No PDF was supplied, so no PDF rendering was possible. The only locator is p. 7, with no study, outcome, sex, country, predictor, or model specified. Source page 7 (printed p. 815) includes multiple distinct pooled effects, heterogeneity tests, country-indicator meta-regressions, sensitivity analyses, and a union-type contrast. No unique target can be assigned from this locator; numeric matching and row-order assignment were not used. Candidate tests on printed p. 815: pooled parental SES effect on first-union timing for women (b minus 0.171, P < 0.01) and men (b minus 0.055, P < 0.01); women cohabitation (b minus 0.069, P < 0.01) and marriage (b minus 0.232, P < 0.01); contrast of marriage versus cohabitation (P < 0.01); cohabitation-prevalence meta-regression (b 0.178; canonical P token 0.0186, with final 6 potentially the note marker; not resolved without PDF), sensitivity excluding Denmark/Sweden (b 0.279, P 0.003); age-norm meta-regression (b minus 0.150, P 0.054), sensitivity excluding Denmark (b minus 0.198, P 0.031); heterogeneity tests also occur. Canonical text encodes negative signs as U+0002 and equality signs as U+00BC; exact evidence preserves these characters. No metric conversion or p-value inference was performed. Sample candidates only: analytic participants 20,495 men and 24,652 women after 4 percent missing-variable exclusions; 211,307 women person-years and 211,769 men person-years; country-level models use countries (25 overall, sensitivity analyses remove specified countries). These are distinct roles, not interchangeable analytic Ns. No sum was assigned because target correspondence is unresolved. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
